tasks.title: Clean Up Codebase and Remove Twitter Template Code
tasks.description: Remove all Twitter extension template code and clean up unused components and dependencies to prepare the codebase for RentEst implementation.
tasks.details:
1. Identify and remove all Twitter-specific components, utilities, and assets
   - Remove components: Posts.js, Profile.js, Carousel.js, Ghost.js, Listings.js, ListingsDetails.js, StarIconComponent.js, Navigation.js, FeedSlider.js, ExtrasCheckboxes.js, ExtrasSwitches.js, Separator.js, Extras.js, ExtrasSection.js, FeedSection.js, NavigationSection.js, AffiliateSection.js
   - Keep and repurpose: FrontdoorPage.js, Search.js, Header.js, Main.js, Container.js, Footer.js, Layout components, Chart components
   - Remove Twitter-specific utilities in chrometab.js and chromeStorage.js
2. Delete unused dependencies from package.json
   - Remove: @chakra-ui/*, @emotion/*, @radix-ui/*, @stitches/react
3. Run npm prune to clean up node_modules
4. Remove Twitter-specific styles and theme elements
   - Update tailwind.config.js - replace Twitter colors (twitterBlue, twitterBgOne, etc.) with RentEst brand colors
   - Update globals.css - replace Twitter CSS variables and color scheme
5. Clean up any Twitter-related configuration files
   - Update manifest.json - change extension name/description
6. Document removed components for reference
   - Update README.md with changes made
7. Ensure the application still builds after cleanup
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the application builds successfully without errors. Check that no Twitter-specific code remains in the codebase. Run linting tools to ensure code quality.

tasks.title: Set Up RentCast API Integration Framework
tasks.description: Create the API service layer for RentCast endpoints and implement secure API key management.
tasks.details:
1. Sign up for RentCast API (free tier - 50 calls/month)
2. Create an API service class with methods for each endpoint
3. Implement secure API key storage using environment variables
4. Set up API request/response interfaces using TypeScript
5. Implement request throttling to respect API rate limits
6. Create error handling utilities for API responses
7. Set up a caching mechanism to reduce API calls
8. Document the API integration for future reference
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests for API service methods. Test API key security. Verify rate limiting functionality works as expected. Test error handling with mocked failed responses.
